did_you_know.text: Did you know? At the beginning of the chapter, David is described as very old and weak: even though they covered him with blankets, he could not get warm.
Did you know? Abishag the Shunammite served David and cared for him, but the text emphasizes that David did not have sexual relations with her.
Did you know? Adonijah did not wait for an official decision from David. Instead, he effectively declared, “I will be king,” and prepared a chariot, horsemen, and fifty men to run ahead of him.
Did you know? Among Solomon’s supporters were Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, and David’s mighty men; they did not join Adonijah.
Did you know? Adonijah invited his brothers and the king’s officials to his coronation feast, but deliberately did not invite Solomon, Nathan, Benaiah, or the mighty men.
Did you know? Nathan the prophet understood that Adonijah’s actions endangered both Bathsheba and Solomon, so he worked with Bathsheba to bring the matter to David’s attention.

Did you know? Bathsheba emphasized to David that Adonijah had held a great feast and invited Joab and Abiathar, but had not invited Solomon—showing that he was attempting to establish a successor without the king’s consent.
Did you know? David ordered Solomon to be crowned at Gihon: Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet were to anoint him, and the people were to acclaim him by shouting, “Long live King Solomon!”
Did you know? At the coronation ceremony, Zadok took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon, while the people blew trumpets and cheered for him as king.

Did you know? After hearing that Solomon had been crowned, Adonijah seized the horns of the altar to seek protection. Solomon did not kill him, but made his release conditional on his loyalty and warned that rebellion would lead to his death.
